## Why the badges

I was genuinely torn about using [Claude Code](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-code) for this website. This is a personal website, a place where I organise the projects I develop in my free time and a way of guiding my own learning, and I was not sure it made sense to have an AI assistant contribute to it.

At the same time, I had a large catalogue of work waiting to be moved here, and not a lot of time to do it all. In the end I came to a compromise: I use Claude where it helps me bring that work online, and I am transparent about it. Every post where an AI assistant was involved carries one of the two badges below, together with a short note on what it did.

## The two badges

:::

```{=html}
<div class="ai-badge-explainer">
  <div class="ai-badge-card">
    <div class="ai-badge ai-badge-assisted">
      <span class="ai-badge-pill"><i class="bi bi-robot ai-badge-icon" aria-hidden="true"></i>AI-assisted</span>
    </div>
    <p><strong>I wrote it, AI helped.</strong> The ideas, the analyses and most of the code are mine. An AI assistant helped with specific parts, for example reviewing the code, fixing bugs, restructuring sections or producing figures.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="ai-badge-card">
    <div class="ai-badge ai-badge-generated">
      <span class="ai-badge-pill"><i class="bi bi-robot ai-badge-icon" aria-hidden="true"></i>AI-generated</span>
    </div>
    <p><strong>AI wrote it, I directed it.</strong> Most of the content was produced by an AI assistant following my direction. I chose the topic, guided the work and reviewed the result.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

::: {.justify}

The note next to each badge says what the AI assistant actually did on that post, as the same badge can cover quite different amounts of help. Posts without a badge were written without AI assistance.

:::
